source.title: ObserverBench: Testing Mechanistic Estimates for Intervention and Control

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present, including appendices; not garbled or cut off.
record.tranche_reason: On GPT-2-small IOI, the study applies mean ablations to head masks drawn from published IOI head groups and evaluates IOI margins/action losses. It reports a qualitative backup-behavior check, but does not reproduce the original whole-circuit faithfulness, completeness, or minimality evaluation.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly says it uses the IOI circuit as a known intervention surface, not to discover a circuit. It states that whole-group ablations reproduce known backup behavior, but gives no separate numerical result for that check. Its mean-effect prediction MAEs and R² compare newly built observers, not the circuit itself, so they are not rows. The main fixed-action results are included as findings about outcomes of ablations on IOI prompts, not as evidence for circuit completeness. Qwen induction-copy and safety results do not test this GPT-2 IOI claim.
record.test_reason: The study uses published IOI head groups in GPT-2-small (name movers, backup and negative name movers) only as an intervention surface for its ObserverBench effect-prediction task. It says so explicitly: 'We do not claim to discover a new circuit.' Its numbers score its own observers: mean-effect MAE, R², and fixed-action loss of the selected masks. The single statement bearing on V2 is a one-sentence sanity check with no group, number or baseline. The authors call it 'a check that the intervention works as intended, not a new mechanistic result.' That is reliance on the finding, not a test of it, so no verdicts are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors use IOI head groups as a known intervention surface and claim no new mechanism. They conclude that pairwise terms improve mean-effect prediction but not the fixed action chosen. Directly predicting prompt-level loss picks lower-loss masks; at t=1 these beat the mean observer and exact no-op. Exact no-op must be included because acting is not always warranted, as at t=0.5.
record.recipe_differences: Uses GPT-2-small IOI and mean head ablations over published head groups, but evaluates fixed-action effect prediction rather than recovering or validating the full circuit against faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
record.method_sensitivity: Action-loss outcomes depend on the target: direct-loss ablation is worse than no-op at t = 0.5, but better at t = 1.0 and t = 1.5. The confirmation reports that direct loss beats no-op on six of eight templates, not uniformly.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-ablation effects of mixed name-mover, backup and negative-name-mover masks are non-additive. Pairwise group or head interaction terms cut held-out mean-effect MAE from 0.486 to 0.395 at budget 160. Effects also vary widely across prompts, so the mean misses most of the action-relevant dispersion.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ablation effects of IOI head groups in GPT-2-small interact non-additively and vary substantially across prompts within a template set.

fits_no_version.finding: For selecting fixed head-ablation masks, predicting prompt-level action loss beats predicting the mean effect: an 18.5% reduction at t=1. Whether any ablation beats no-op depends on the target: worse at t=0.5, better at t=1.0 and t=1.5.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For GPT-2-small IOI head-ablation candidates, direct action-loss prediction selects lower-loss fixed interventions than mean-effect prediction; the value of acting is target-dependent.

fits_no_version.finding: Clean GPT-2-small IO-versus-subject accuracy is 0.867 overall on eight new templates (worst template 0.578). On the eight canonical templates it is 0.977 (worst 0.953). This is behavioural template sensitivity with no circuit attribution.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: GPT-2-small's IOI behaviour degrades on some non-canonical templates.

record.problems: The study does not test the complete IOI circuit or its faithfulness, completeness, or minimality. The backup-behavior check is qualitative in the paper text. The first fixed-action IOI comparison lacked exact no-op and failed its clean-task gate; the confirmation was selected after a pilot-informed screening. The confirmation gain over no-op was not uniform across templates.
record.rows_left_out: Observer-comparison metrics such as mean-effect MAE and R² were left out because they score the paper's new prediction methods rather than the IOI circuit's behavior. Qwen induction-copy and safety-triage results were left out because they do not test the GPT-2-small IOI claim.

untested.parts: The full 26-head, 7-class circuit and its faithfulness, completeness and minimality are not evaluated. Only three published head groups (13 heads) are used.
Backup takeover after name-mover ablation is asserted only as an unquantified sanity check. No group, magnitude or comparison is reported.
No other model, size or checkpoint is tested for IOI. The Qwen task is induction-copy with a different head panel.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics for recovering the circuit.
Circuit faithfulness or completeness is not measured under different ablations, metrics or prompt distributions.
Templates vary, but the paper does not test whether the same components carry IOI across them.

missing.what: Clean IO-versus-subject accuracy by template set: 0.867 overall and worst 0.578 on new templates, versus 0.977 overall and worst 0.953 on canonical templates. This is behavioural context for prompt-variant robustness; no row records it.

record.verdict_notes: I reclassified the study from tests/T1 to uses_without_test/T4 and dropped the reader's V2 'supports' label. The only V2-relevant content is an unquantified one-sentence sanity check. Of the IOI references, only arXiv:2211.00593 [16] is the original source; the others are cited prior work. The Qwen and safety sections are irrelevant to this claim.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not test the complete 26-head, 7-class circuit, or its faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria.
The study reports a qualitative whole-group-ablation check of known backup behavior, but not a detailed quantitative takeover analysis after ablating the main name-mover heads.
No test of the same IOI circuit in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods or ablation types for recovering the circuit.
The study compares effect-prediction and action-loss objectives for IOI ablations, but does not measure circuit faithfulness or completeness across ablation types, metrics, or prompt distributions.
The study uses multiple IOI templates, but does not test whether the same circuit carries IOI across name orders, more names, or prompt variants.
